subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should #39248 be fixed as a narrow sandbox startup/diagnostics bug, folded into the broader subagent lifecycle contract from #58776, or held until live Docker reproduction proves the exact failing phase?
rationale: Current source proves the reported path is real, but the overlapping lifecycle work and missing live Docker proof make the permanent contract and fix boundary a maintainer choice rather than a safe autonomous repair.

options.title: Require live sandbox repro first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a live Docker `non-main` `sessions_spawn` reproduction that identifies the failing phase before authorizing a fix PR.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle contract
options.body: Treat #39248 as a sandbox-triggered instance of #58776 and require the lifecycle design to prove startup failure, first progress, and completion behavior for sandboxed subagents too.

options.title: Patch narrow sandbox diagnostics
options.body: Authorize a focused fix that records sandbox backend/bootstrap failures into run/session state without adding the broader first-progress lifecycle API yet.

recommendation.title: Require live sandbox repro first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a live Docker `non-main` `sessions_spawn` reproduction that identifies the failing phase before authorizing a fix PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad work across gateway agent routing, session lifecycle, and sandbox context surfaces, making this the best available owner for the contract decision.
